description: The bar chart illustrates the percentage point difference in morphosyntactic probing performance between two multilingual BERT models — mBERT and XLM-R — across four different hidden layer configurations, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The horizontal axis lists the configurations: “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” representing variations in probe architecture (hidden layer sizes and activation functions). The vertical axis, labeled “% point difference,” ranges from –0.2 to +0.2, indicating the relative performance advantage (positive) or disadvantage (negative) of XLM-R over mBERT. Each configuration has two adjacent bars: light gray for mBERT and dark gray for XLM-R, with the bar height reflecting the model’s performance difference relative to a baseline or each other. For “hidden:[50], linear,” mBERT shows a negative difference (~–0.15), while XLM-R is slightly negative (~–0.05). In “hidden:[], linear,” both models perform positively, with XLM-R (~+0.20) outperforming mBERT (~+0.09). For “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is negative (~–0.12), and XLM-R is slightly positive (~+0.03). In “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” both are negative, with mBERT at ~–0.18 and XLM-R at ~–0.13. The chart visually suggests that XLM-R generally outperforms mBERT, especially in the “hidden:[], linear” configuration, while both models underperform in deeper ReLU-based probes.
